We will analyze a large number of non-fiction representations of the world and its people, focusing on a range of documentary styles and genres and rooting this diversity in its various historical and social contexts, as well as considering the ethical and aesthetic aspects of documentaries. The course primarily considers documentary film, but we will also explore the genre through other media forms, including audio productions, allowing students to develop skills useful in an increasingly multimodal culture. Assessment includes a presentation, the production of a very short documentary item, an essay-type exam and several small homework assignments on Moodle. Input to help shape this course is highly appreciated. Contribution is limited to the actual taught subject and assessment. No whole Maastricht module, research trajectory or professional equivalence claimed.
MCCMEDI312.topics: Documentary definition, modes and ethics; Early documentary and city symphonies; Soviet filmmaking; European documentary traditions; Direct cinema and cinéma vérité; Audio and public-affairs documentary; Propaganda and advocacy; Historical and ethnographic documentary; Nature documentary; Mockumentary; Interactive and autobiographical documentary; Documentary aesthetics

options.label: Culture, history, philosophy and the arts
options.concept: Study how cultural ideas and forms change over time through history, philosophy, literature and the visual arts. Use close reading, qualitative inquiry and historical sources to investigate representation, public culture and the institutions that shape them.

options.label: Digital culture, media and ethics
options.concept: Study how changing technologies shape cultural expression, representation and public debate. Analyse film, screens and experimental forms, and examine AI ethics and the social effects of automation. Data science and machine learning provide technical context.

options.label: Environmental culture, media and governance
options.concept: Study how films, public communication and social movements shape responses to environmental change. Examine environmental justice, law and sustainability governance, using climate science, water management and regional research to ground the cultural questions.
traceOverrides: examines nonfiction representation, including nature documentary, through documentary history, ethics and production

analysis: The closest option combines arts and literature with philosophical argument, cultural and historical cases, political ideas and documentary and ethnographic inquiry. American Century supports research questions and evidence evaluation through a substantial historical paper. Digital culture combines media archaeology, film, documentary, adaptation, persuasion and experimental communication with technology ethics, AI in the economy and technical context. Creative Communication Laboratory replaces the digital option’s general law course and adds close reading, poetry, performance and hybrid creative work. Business & Economy in the Age of AI stays as evidenced discussion of automation, inequality and regulation. The environmental option combines films and environmental representation, climate debate, justice, water governance and political and legal institutions with documented scientific context. The Documentary replaces its broad Western philosophy survey and adds nonfiction representation, nature documentary and practical production. The partner-defined regional investigation occurs in term one. The candidates differ each way by 12, 15 and 18 courses, respectively. Related themes of marginalised representation, democracy and social norms are present in concrete course content but do not add a distinct fourth plan. Course-level evidence includes bounded roles for descriptions of Greek Archaeology, Researching the American Century, Database Management Systems, environmental justice and climate communication. No single scheduled course supplies Maastricht’s dedicated proposal or required 16 EC thesis.
